text:
Sam: quick check-in on the response envelope work — customer asks: per-call token breakouts, tracing, and clear function-call fields. Want to align before we commit to SDK changes.
Jo: my vote: smallest possible surface that covers all modes. flat keys avoid accidental nested parsing in some languages.
Iris: agreed on flat, but still need a mode tag so we don't misinterpret fields (embedding_dim only for embeddings, rerank_score only for rerank). propose mode: chat|completion|embedding|rerank.
Marco: on token fields: tokens_in/tokens_out are compact. Also include tokens_total for quick queries.
Sam: +1 to tokens_in/out/total. We should also provide cost_usd as a float string in the envelope. customers asked for it for immediate billing joins.
Jo: tracing: canonical trace_id (hex-128) we emit. Accept upstream request_id header and echo it back as request_id when provided. We'll document that request_id is optional and not generated by us.
Iris: function calls: we saw confusion with function_call object in older SDKs. Flatten to function_name (string), function_invoked (bool), function_args_truncated (bool). Keep booleans simple.
Marco: embeddings: include embedding_dim (int), vector_present (bool). We should not emit vectors in telemetry by default. If a customer opts in, we can add vector_in_response: true.
Sam: also consider privacy: do not log or export raw vectors by default. Add a flag vector_export_opt_in in Console per project.
Jo: example minimal envelope for chat (for docs):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-v2",
  "mode": "chat",
  "trace_id": "9f8b7a6c5d4e3f2a1b0c9d8e7f6a5b4",
  "request_id": "acme-2024-11-12-42",
  "tokens_in": 28,
  "tokens_out": 110,
  "tokens_total": 138,
  "cost_usd": 0.0027,
  "function_name": "extract_entities",
  "function_invoked": false,
  "function_args_truncated": false
}
```
Iris: embedding example:
```json
{
  "model": "embed-lite-1",
  "mode": "embedding",
  "trace_id": "...",
  "tokens_in": 15,
  "tokens_out": 0,
  "tokens_total": 15,
  "cost_usd": 0.0006,
  "embedding_dim": 1536,
  "vector_present": false
}
```
Marco: rollout acceptance checklist (proposal):
- Docs with examples for each mode (chat/comp/embed/rerank) 
- Console exposes per-request tokens and cost_usd within 24h
- Canary: 3 pilot customers for two weeks, monitor quality regressions and parsing issues
- SLOs: 95th <= 250ms for short chat, 99th <= 450ms for non-batched requests; measurable in Console
- SDK backward compat: server accepts requestId and request_id, emits canonical request_id in responses
Sam: deploy-bot, can you reserve canary capacity?
deploy-bot: Canary capacity reserved: 1.5x baseline in prod-eu for 2024-11-05T04:00:00Z -> 2024-11-19T04:00:00Z.
Jo: migration note: accept common aliases server-side for 6 weeks (requestId/request_id/request-id) and emit canonical names. Include a changelog entry and a migration guide for customers parsing fields.
Iris: perf/token impact study: I'll run a quick simulation comparing short keys (tokens_in) vs long keys (token_usage_input) on 10k calls. estimate: ~2 tokens saved per call on average from key length reduction and JSON overhead. I'll post numbers here.
Marco: ops note: some enterprise customers will require dedicated routing to meet the 99th p95 targets. Add a line to the runbook.
Sam: action items: Jo opens schema PR with flat keys + examples (due Tue EOD). Iris posts token/perf sims (due Wed). Marco drafts canary runbook + ops notes (due Wed).
Jo: will include example SDK snips for Python/TS showing how to read fields.
Iris: small UX ask: include a human-readable epoch timestamp created_at in the envelope to help customers with joins. short key: created_at_unix.
Marco: fine, as long as it's unix seconds (int).
Sam: ok locking on these fields unless someone raises a blocking concern by Tue noon. otherwise we proceed with PR and docs updates. :thumbsup:
